cohort: The study analyzed 11,770 births from Cruzeiro do Sul, Acre, Brazil, between 2018 and 2021.
finding: The prevalence of cesarean sections in Cruzeiro do Sul, Acre, from 2018-2021 was 49.96%, exceeding international recommendations, and was influenced by maternal and neonatal factors, as well as the pandemic context.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was more common among mothers over 40 years of age, white, who worked outside the home, and who had undergone a previous cesarean section, while it was less common among mothers who worked in agriculture, were single, or had few prenatal visits, with low birth weight and Apgar scores also associated.
birth_weight: Low birth weight was identified as a characteristic associated with cesarean section.
